title: Find your rhythm
objective: Introduce Mojito Metallique through a playful dance-studio break, then turn the attention into a clear two-item purchase action.
casting: One adult Filipino woman. Use the bottle with the white/cream scent label, black MOJITO METALLIQUE lettering, golden-yellow liquid, and fitted black cap. Any additional visible talent must also be female, although this production is designed for one performer.
description: Soft, creamy sweetness with a light fruity glow.
scene: A sunlit dance-studio doorway with a coral bench and a cream wall. The performer has just finished a casual rehearsal and is resetting her headphones. The story is about her personal style and enjoyment of music; fragrance is not presented as a deodorant or a way to hide sweat.
styling: Butter-yellow cotton tee, dark denim, small plain gold hoops, natural hair in a loose ponytail. One cobalt headphone set around her neck. Use yellow, coral, cream and a small burgundy accent. No mirror in the frame.
props: One exact capped Mojito Metallique bottle; one headphone set; coral bench; simple unbranded tote placed out of the hero crop. Keep the bottle label dry and clean. Do not add mint, lime or cocktails based on the product name.
lighting: Place the bench beside a large window or open door. Let daylight skim the bottle from one side and bounce a white board toward the face. Keep skin warm and natural; retain the true yellow liquid instead of adding a strong orange filter.
camera: Film vertically. Use an eye-level medium shot for personality, a tighter hand-and-bottle shot for identity, and one low waist-level step shot for movement. Keep the camera steady during the label close-up. Record the dance action with a little space around elbows so a 4:5 crop works.
performance: Ask her to react to a familiar beat and smile at a point beside the camera. Use a small shoulder bounce and one easy step, not a full choreographed routine. Bring the bottle toward the camera only slightly so its scale remains believable.
sound: Use a licensed upbeat instrumental with a light rhythmic groove. Record a real headphone tap, soft shoe step and tote rustle. Keep these below the voiceover; do not use a recognisable commercial song without the appropriate rights.
